steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Genre shapes your approach: portraiture focuses on character and expression; landscape on space and atmosphere; documentary on truth and narrative.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Developing a personal style means making consistent creative choices — not just about subject matter but about how you see and photograph.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Fine art photography prioritises the photographer's creative vision over documentation — the image is the artwork, not a record.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Understanding genre conventions helps you work within them intentionally or break them deliberately for creative effect.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring photographic genres and styles. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with photographic genres and styles. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with photographic genres and styles. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to photographic genres and styles, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined o | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
